qs.q: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\lambda-1&6&0\\1&\lambda-2&0\end{bmatrix}$ be the augmented matrix of a linear system. If the system has infinitely many solutions, then $\lambda\neq$ ----
e: The last column is zero, so the system is homogeneous: it is always consistent, and it has infinitely many solutions exactly when it has a nontrivial solution.
Swap $R_1\leftrightarrow R_2$: $\begin{bmatrix}1&\lambda-2&0\\\lambda-1&6&0\end{bmatrix}$.
$R_2\to R_2-(\lambda-1)R_1$: second row becomes $[\,0\ \ 6-(\lambda-1)(\lambda-2)\ \ 0\,]$.
$6-(\lambda-1)(\lambda-2)=-(\lambda^2-3\lambda-4)=-(\lambda-4)(\lambda+1)$.
The system has a free variable (infinitely many solutions) only if this entry is $0$, i.e. $\lambda=4$ or $\lambda=-1$.
For $\lambda=1$ the entry equals $6\neq0$, so only the trivial solution exists. Hence $\lambda$ can never be $1$: $\lambda\neq1$.

qs.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&6c&0\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}$ is the augmented matrix of a linear system and $c\neq1$, then the system has ----
e: The last column is zero, so the system is homogeneous and always has the trivial solution (it can never be inconsistent).
Swap $R_1\leftrightarrow R_2$: $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0\\3&6c&0\end{bmatrix}$.
$R_2\to R_2-3R_1$: $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0\\0&6c-6&0\end{bmatrix}$.
Since $c\neq1$, $6c-6\neq0$, so row 2 gives $y=0$ and then row 1 gives $x=0$.
Only the trivial solution exists, so the system has exactly one solution.

qs.q: $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&5\\-2&3&6\end{bmatrix}$ is the augmented matrix of a linear system. If the system is solved by Gaussian elimination, then in step 2 $a_{22}=$ ----
e: Gaussian elimination steps: (1) find the leftmost nonzero column, (2) interchange rows if the top entry of that column is zero, (3) scale the top row to get a leading 1, (4) clear the entries below the leading 1.
Step 1: the leftmost nonzero column is column 1.
Step 2: the top entry is already $1\neq0$, so no interchange is needed and the matrix does not change.
After step 2 the matrix is still $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&5\\-2&3&6\end{bmatrix}$, so $a_{22}=3$.
(The entry changes only in step 4, where $R_2\to R_2+2R_1$ gives $a_{22}=7$.)
In row-echelon form every nonzero row must begin with a leading 1, and any all-zero rows must be at the bottom.
If $d\neq0$, row 2 is a nonzero row, so its first nonzero entry $d$ must be a leading 1, hence $d=1$.
If $d=0$, row 2 is a zero row at the bottom, which is allowed.
Any other value, such as $d=2$, violates the leading-1 condition. So $d=0$ or $d=1$.

qs.q: $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&5\\-3&1&6\end{bmatrix}$ is the augmented matrix of a linear system. If the system is solved by <u>Gaussian elimination</u>, then in <u>step 3</u> the second row of the matrix is ----
e: Step 1: the leftmost nonzero column is column 1.
Step 2: the top entry is $1\neq0$, so no row interchange is needed.
Step 3: the top entry is $a=1$, so multiplying the first row by $1/a=1$ changes nothing.
Rows 1 and 2 are unchanged after step 3, so row 2 is still $[-3\ \ 1\ \ 6]$.
Only in step 4 ($R_2\to R_2+3R_1$) does row 2 become $[0\ \ 7\ \ 21]$.
